requirements_xml:
<requirements_list>
  <requirement id="R1">
    <category>Existence</category>
    <description>The `display` CSS property must exist and accept a `<display-inside>` keyword value in its syntax.</description>
    <spec_quote>| Name: | display |
| Value: | [ [<display-outside>](#typedef-display-outside) || [<display-inside>](#typedef-display-inside) ] | [<display-listitem>](#typedef-display-listitem) | [<display-internal>](#typedef-display-internal) | [<display-box>](#typedef-display-box) | [<display-legacy>](#typedef-display-legacy) |</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R2">
    <category>Existence</category>
    <description>The `flow-root` keyword must be supported as a valid `<display-inside>` value for the `display` CSS property.</description>
    <spec_quote><display-inside>   = flow | flow-root | table | flex | grid | ruby</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R3">
    <category>Common Use Cases</category>
    <description>The display property must accept flow-root as a valid inner display type keyword value.</description>
    <spec_quote><display-inside>   = flow | flow-root | table | flex | grid | ruby</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R4">
    <category>Common Use Cases</category>
    <description>When display: flow-root is specified without an outer display type keyword, the element's outer display type must default to block.</description>
    <spec_quote>If a [<display-inside>](#typedef-display-inside) value is specified but [<display-outside>](#typedef-display-outside) is omitted,
the element’s [outer display type](#outer-display-type) defaults to [block](#valdef-display-block)—​except for [ruby](#valdef-display-ruby), which defaults to [inline](#valdef-display-inline).</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R5">
    <category>Common Use Cases</category>
    <description>Because display: flow-root has an outer display type of block, the element must generate a box that is block-level when placed in flow layout.</description>
    <spec_quote>block
:   The element generates a box that is
    block-level
    when placed in [flow layout](#flow-layout).</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R6">
    <category>Common Use Cases</category>
    <description>A non-replaced element with display: flow-root must generate a block container box.</description>
    <spec_quote>flow-root
:   The element generates a [block container](#block-container) box</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R7">
    <category>Common Use Cases</category>
    <description>A non-replaced element with display: flow-root must lay out its contents using flow layout.</description>
    <spec_quote>The element generates a [block container](#block-container) box,
    and lays out its contents using [flow layout](#flow-layout).</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R8">
    <category>Common Use Cases</category>
    <description>A non-replaced element with display: flow-root must always establish a new block formatting context for its contents.</description>
    <spec_quote>It always establishes a new [block formatting context](#block-formatting-context) for its contents.</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R9">
    <category>Common Use Cases</category>
    <description>Because display: flow-root establishes an independent block formatting context, the box must grow to fully contain its internal floated descendants so their layout effects do not escape its formatting context.</description>
    <spec_quote>in a [block formatting context](#block-formatting-context),
    floated boxes affect the layout of surrounding boxes.
    But their effects do not escape their [formatting context](#formatting-context):
    the box establishing their formatting context grows to fully contain them</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R10">
    <category>Common Use Cases</category>
    <description>Because display: flow-root establishes an independent block formatting context, floated boxes from outside the flow-root element must not protrude into or affect the layout of contents inside the box.</description>
    <spec_quote>floats from outside that box
    are not allowed to protrude into and affect the contents
    inside the box.</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R11">
    <category>Common Use Cases</category>
    <description>Because display: flow-root establishes a new block formatting context, margins must not collapse across its formatting context boundaries with its descendants, itself, or outside sibling elements.</description>
    <spec_quote>margins do not collapse across [formatting context](#formatting-context) boundaries.</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R12">
    <category>Common Use Cases</category>
    <description>As a block container, a display: flow-root box containing mixed block-level and inline-level content must generate anonymous block boxes so that it directly contains only block-level boxes participating in its block formatting context.</description>
    <spec_quote>A block container either contains only inline-level boxes
    participating in an [inline formatting context](#inline-formatting-context),
    or contains only block-level boxes
    participating in a [block formatting context](#block-formatting-context)
    (possibly generating anonymous block boxes to ensure this constraint,
    as defined in CSS2§9.2.1.1).</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R13">
    <category>Common Use Cases</category>
    <description>As a block container, a display: flow-root box that contains only inline-level content must establish a new inline formatting context for those contents.</description>
    <spec_quote>A block container that contains only inline-level content
    establishes a new [inline formatting context](#inline-formatting-context).</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R14">
    <category>Integration</category>
    <description>The `display: flow-root` declaration must not apply to `::first-line` or `::first-letter` pseudo-elements.</description>
    <spec_quote>None of the properties in this module apply to the `::first-line` or `::first-letter` pseudo-elements.</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R15">
    <category>Integration</category>
    <description>The `display` property with `flow-root` must not be animatable by CSS animations or transitions.</description>
    <spec_quote>| Animation type: | not animatable |</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R16">
    <category>Integration</category>
    <description>Setting `display: flow-root` on an element must not alter the element's document-language semantics.</description>
    <spec_quote>The [display](#propdef-display) property has no effect on an element’s semantics:
these are defined by the document language and *are not affected by CSS*.</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R17">
    <category>Integration</category>
    <description>Setting `display: flow-root` on an element must only affect visual layout and must not suppress or alter the aural/speech output or interactivity of the element and its descendants.</description>
    <spec_quote>Aside from the [none](#valdef-display-none) value,
which also affects the aural/speech output [[CSS-SPEECH-1]](#biblio-css-speech-1 "CSS Speech Module Level 1")
and interactivity of an element and its descendants,
the display property only affects visual layout</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R18">
    <category>Integration</category>
    <description>When an element with `display: flow-root` is inlinified by a layout effect (such as containment in a ruby container), its computed outer display type must be set to `inline` while preserving its `flow-root` inner display type.</description>
    <spec_quote>Some layout effects require blockification
or inlinification of the box type,
which sets the box’s computed [outer display type](#outer-display-type)
to [block](#valdef-display-block) or [inline](#valdef-display-inline) (respectively).</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R19">
    <category>Integration</category>
    <description>When an element with `display: flow-root` is blockified by a layout effect (such as floating, absolute positioning, or having a flex or grid parent), its computed outer display type must remain `block` while preserving its `flow-root` inner display type.</description>
    <spec_quote>Some layout effects require blockification
or inlinification of the box type,
which sets the box’s computed [outer display type](#outer-display-type)
to [block](#valdef-display-block) or [inline](#valdef-display-inline) (respectively).</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R20">
    <category>Integration</category>
    <description>A `display: flow-root` box must grow to fully contain internal floated descendant boxes so their layout effects do not escape its block formatting context.</description>
    <spec_quote>the box establishing their formatting context grows to fully contain them</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R21">
    <category>Integration</category>
    <description>Floated boxes outside a `display: flow-root` element must not protrude into or affect the layout of contents inside the `display: flow-root` box.</description>
    <spec_quote>floats from outside that box
    are not allowed to protrude into and affect the contents
    inside the box.</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R22">
    <category>Integration</category>
    <description>CSS Exclusions must be able to affect content across the independent formatting context boundary established by a `display: flow-root` box.</description>
    <spec_quote>Exclusions are able to affect content across [independent formatting context](#independent-formatting-context) boundaries.</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R23">
    <category>Integration</category>
    <description>A `run-in` sequence immediately followed by a `display: flow-root` box must not be inserted as direct children of that box, because a `display: flow-root` box establishes a new block formatting context.</description>
    <spec_quote>If a [run-in sequence](#run-in-sequence) is immediately followed by a block box
  that does not establish a new [block formatting context](#block-formatting-context),
  it is inserted as direct children of that block box</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
</requirements_list>
